title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the neighbouring pages: Grothendieck is computing S_0 T_G, a torsor of 'base-point-like' data attached to a stratum of type G in the Teichmüller tower. Here G = G_Q is the dual graph of the maximally degenerate stable curve in \bar M_{0,4}. It has two vertices s ∈ S (S ≃ the two diagonals of the combinatorial square Q). Each vertex carries three branches Â_s = Δ_s ⊔ {s̃}: two free legs, which are the endpoints of the diagonal Δ_s and are marked points in I = vertices of Q, plus one half-edge s̃. The two half-edges s̃ form the single internal edge. E_s = cyclic orders on Â_s ≃ Δ_s, and E(G) = ∏_s Δ_s ≃ A(Q) (the sides of Q) is a torsor under γ(G) = {±1}^S. S_0 T_G is obtained by lifting this torsor through the extension 0→Z^S --2--> Z^S→{±1}^S→0, which gives a Z^S-torsor. It is then pushed along a homomorphism Z^S → Z^Â. Read geometrically, this map sends 'half-twists at vertices' to twists along legs and edges.

This page makes that homomorphism explicit as a composite Z^S → Z^{\vec Â} → Z^Â.
- The first arrow is obtained contravariantly (pull-back) from the origin map or: \vec Â → S, where \vec Â is the set of oriented half-edges.
- The second is obtained covariantly (push-forward, i.e. summation over fibres) from \vec Â → Â ≃ \vec Â/σ, where σ reverses orientation.

Because Â ≃ I ⊔ {one internal edge}, Z^Â ≃ Z^I × Z, and the map splits into two components:
- Z^S → Z^I, the pull-back along the degree-2 map I → S (each marked point goes to the vertex carrying it);
- Z^S → Z, the sum map. The internal edge has its two orientations based at the two distinct vertices, so its coefficient is n_{s1} + n_{s2}.
errors: No mathematical error. The decomposition is correct: legs have only one orientation-origin, while the internal edge collects contributions from both vertices, giving the sum.
Minor ambiguity: the page writes Â for both the half-edge set and its quotient by σ. The intended meaning (Â = \vec Â/σ as the target) is clear from context.

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the vertex lattice to the edge/leg lattice of a stable graph: pull back along the origin map of oriented half-edges, then push forward along the quotient by orientation reversal. Interpreted as the relation between vertex (half-)twists and Dehn twists along legs and edges.
ideas.modern_name: Incidence map Z^{V(G)} → Z^{E(G)∪L(G)}; relation between rotations of pants and Dehn twists (cf. half-twists in the Teichmüller groupoid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorics of stable graphs; Teichmüller-groupoid setting: Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower with base points at maximally degenerate curves, but not this explicit computation.

ideas.what: Computing the torsor S_0 T_G for the maximally degenerate stratum of M_{0,4}, by pushing out the orientation torsor E(G) through the doubling extension Z^S → Z^S → {±1}^S.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidified / quasi-tangential base points at maximal degeneration

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, routine bookkeeping step: the explicit form of the incidence homomorphism used in a torsor construction from the previous page. It is correct and elementary, and the surrounding ideas are well developed in the later Teichmüller-tower literature.
